In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology to predict the performance of a GIS.
the development and application of a methodology for estimating the performance of GIS hardware and software.
the performance evaluation and work load estimation of GISs.

GIS performance can be estimated accurately, but that it is not possible to make such a statement with any certainty about GIS workloads.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance model can be used to predict the resource requirements of a GIS, given the number of tasks to be executed and their characteristics.
it has been possible to develop a formal approach for the evaluation of GIS hardware and software, and that it is feasible to implement this in a form which is useful to the GIS user.
it is possible to estimate GIS system performance and workloads with a high degree of accuracy, and to predict system resource requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of GIS software is not a function of hardware alone, and that performance evaluation is a necessary step in the process of acquiring GIS hardware and/or software.
it is possible to develop a formal, quantitative, model of GIS performance that can be used to estimate resource utilization and work-load for GIS projects.
it is possible to develop an understanding of the resource utilization of GIS systems, and to use this knowledge to make better decisions about the acquisition process.
